course_name_original: Retos y Tendencias en los Sistemas de Recolección e Interconexión de Energía Renovable
course_name_en: Challenges and Trends in Renewable Energy Harvesting and Interconnection Systems
prerequisites: It is recommended that the student has passed all the previous subjects in the degree.

learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity for originality in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context.
That students know how to apply acquired knowledge and problem-solving skills in new or unfamiliar environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their area of study.

That students are able to integrate knowledge and face the complexity of making judgments based on information that, being incomplete or limited, includes reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
That students know how to communicate their conclusions and the ultimate knowledge and reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences in a clear and unambiguous way.
That students possess the learning skills that will enable them to continue studying in a way that will be largely self-directed or autonomous.

Write, interpret scientifically and communicate orally, to specialized audiences, documents in the field of the master's master lines (electric power systems, electric and hybrid vehicles, energy efficiency and renewable energies).
Knowing the main multidisciplinary scientific journals focused on the master lines of the master, as well as the main R+D+i centers (public or private) relevant to these lines.
Identify the aspects of technical design that depend to a greater extent on strategic, socio-political, economic and environmental conditioning factors.
Skills related to teamwork, recognizing different roles within a group and different ways of organizing research teams.
Ability to manage information: search, analysis and synthesis of the specific technical information.
Ability to assimilate and communicate information in English concerning technical
Ability to plan and organize work
Skills for critical reasoning, making decisions and making judgments based on information that include reflecting on social and ethical responsibilities of professional activity
Skills for initiative, entreprenourship, quality and results achievements
Identify the technical-economic norms and regulations of different areas (local, regional, national, European, etc.) applicable to electric power systems.

Knowing and analyzing the energy structures and technologies that allow to ensure the coverage of the determined demand, analyzing the future energy needs and the possible technological solutions, taking into account criteria of efficiency, security, supply guarantee and environmental implications.
Know the emerging technologies of application in new electrical systems.
Understand the operation of renewable energy collection and interconnection technologies, and be able to design complex coordination strategies for their integration in modern power systems.
Critically analyze the evolution of the electricity sector, both from the technological point of view, as well as from the economic, sociological and environmental point of view.
Application of the concepts to the practical case of offshore wind power generation plants.

syllabus_topics: Conventional generation vs. renewables and CHP
The electricity sector and the environment
The concept of sustainable development from an environmental and socio-economic point of view. Implications for environmental impact assessment.
Comparison of various energy conversion technology alternatives in relation to sustainable development.
Climate effects and environmental impact assessment derived from different energy conversion strategies.
Implications in the design of power systems according to their environmental impact.
Application to the practical case of energy harvesting and interconnection systems in offshore wind generation plants.
Medium voltage harvesting systems for offshore wind (wiring and connection technologies, associated circuit configurations)
High voltage interconnection systems for offshore wind (substations, high voltage lines, regulation and grid codes, etc.)
teaching_methods: Extensive use of computer aid tools for problem resolution
assessment_rules: Students will be evaluated according to percentages for written exams (15% to 40%), oral exams (15% to 40%), works and projects (20% to 50%), practical cases (10% to 30%), and observation techniques (10% to 20%). The exact percentages for each component will be specified at the beginning of the sessions. Non-attendance evaluation methods may be included if health conditions require it.
bibliography: All references and resources will be provided by the faculty.
